summary.text: Anna Graff is the Democratic candidate for Utah House of Representatives District 12 in the November 3, 2026 general election, in which she faces incumbent Mike Schultz (R).

In a Ballotpedia survey, she described a background in community service and work at a county extension office, and named water and air protection, affordability and government transparency as her priorities.

paragraphs.text: Anna Graff said in a Ballotpedia survey that she was a 4-H member as a child, became a county museum administrator at age 17, and has served on her city planning commission.

She said she later returned to work at her County Extension Office, where she worked with county commissioners, youth development, 4-H and community nutrition programs, and agriculture and horticulture specialists.
Graff also said she is a single parent of a child with special needs.
Graff listed three key campaign messages.
The first is reporting requirements, with enforcement, for industries that use or affect water and air, including ending legal exemptions that keep water use confidential.
The second is addressing rising costs through housing access and more efficient utility use.
The third is transparency and accountability, including mandatory recusals, tighter consequences for concealing conflicts of interest, and campaign donation limits.
